==SynopsisWhat is Xorqen?==
Xorqen is a small family of models made by the Xorqen project.
When Mizuki Hijiri transferred into a new school, hoping for a peaceful high school life. That did not occur instead she met the infamous Hero Club, a group of students affected by [[chūnibyō|chuuibyou]] syndrome. Her new friends, [[User:ClueBot NG|Yamato Noda]] a superhero fan and an athlete, [[Kriesha Chu|Tomoki Takashima]] 2D-girls obsessed [[otaku]], [[BTS|Kazuhiro Nakamura]] a supposed forbidden union of a demon and an angel, and [[Rei Ami|Rei Tsukumo]] a self-proclaimed schemer. The [[Android (operating system)|Hero Club]] decided that Mizuki is one of their own and involve her in their activities to help out other students with their problems.
They are fine-tuned on <ref name="Qwen">Say you want the moon
Watch me learn to fly
Ain't no mountain you could point to
I wouldn't climb
It's crazy, but it's true
There's nothing I won't do
I'd risk it all for you

{{Please leave this line alone (sandbox heading)}} ==NASCAR Busch Grand National Series== In 1982, Thomas Brothers Racing was founded. They opened the team with racing the #0 Valvoline Oldsmobile full-time, with Mike Alexander behind the wheel, and multiple one-off self-sponsored races with veteran drivers Tommy Gale and Jim Vandiver driving the #50. In 1983, Thomas Brothers opened a second full-time Busch series car, using the #50, to be driven by newly signed driver Rick Mast, who was winless last season, but won multiple poles. Mike Alexander returned after a 2-win season to drive the #0 again. Thomas Brothers also ran 8 races with the #25 in a collaboration with Junior Johnson & Associates and Joe Millikan, the 1982 Cup Series Champion. ====Car No. 0 results==== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; font-size:75%" |- ! {{Please leave this line alone (sandbox heading)}} ==NASCAR Busch Grand National Series== In 1982, Thomas Brothers Racing was founded. They opened the team with racing the #0 Valvoline Oldsmobile full-time, with Mike Alexander behind the wheel, and multiple one-off self-sponsored races with veteran drivers Tommy Gale and Jim Vandiver driving the #50. In 1983, Thomas Brothers opened a second full-time Busch series car, using the #50, to be driven by newly signed driver Rick Mast, who was winless last season, but won multiple poles. Mike Alexander returned after a 2-win season to drive the #0 again. '''Mawlana Abul Kalam Azad''' (Bengali: মাওলানা আবুল কালাম আজাদ; born 4 November 1964)
is a Bangladeshi Islamic scholar and politician serving as a Member of Parliament
for the [[Khulna-6]] (Koyra–Paikgacha) constituency. He is a member of
[[Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami]] and was elected to the
[[13th Jatiya Sangsad]] in the general election of 12 February 2026.

==Early Life and Family Background==

Abul Kalam Azad was born on 4 November 1964 into an influential Muslim family
in Guriyabari, under No. 6 Koyra Union, Koyra Upazila, [[Khulna District]].
His ancestors were zamindars (hereditary landowners). He is the second of eight
siblings. His father, Alhaj Akkash Ali Laskar, was a devout and socially
influential figure in the local community.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.abulkalamazad.info/about
 |title=Abul Kalam Azad – Full Biography
 |publisher=abulkalamazad.info
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

==Education==

From childhood, his family instilled the values of community service and
dedication to the welfare of society through self-education.

|-

|-

|-

|-

He received a scholarship in the Dakhil examination. He later enrolled in
Political Science at Jagannath College (now [[Jagannath University]]) in Dhaka,
but was unable to complete the degree due to his political activities.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.abulkalamazad.info/about
 |title=Abul Kalam Azad – Full Biography
 |publisher=abulkalamazad.info
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

==Political Career==

===Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir (1981–1993)===

In 1981, while a Fazil-level student, Azad joined [[Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir]].
He became active in Khulna student politics in 1982 and continued in Dhaka
from 1983 to 1993.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.abulkalamazad.info/about
 |title=Abul Kalam Azad – Full Biography
 |publisher=abulkalamazad.info
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

Positions held within Chhatra Shibir:

* 1985–1986: President, Madrasa-i-Alia Dhaka Branch
* 1987–1989: Zonal In-charge, Dhaka Metropolitan; Central Convener, Bangladesh Madrasa Student Movement Council
* 1989–1991: Secretary, Dhaka Metropolitan South
* 1991–1992: Central Office Secretary
* 1993: Central Baitul Mal (Treasury) Secretary

===Anti-Autocracy Movement===

On 10 January 1986, while serving as branch president at Dhaka Alia Madrasa,
he was attacked and injured during an assault on Chhatra Shibir members.
In 1985, he played a leading national role in protests against a magistrate
in Chapai Nawabganj who had ordered the confiscation of a copy of the Quran.
He was subjected to police violence on several occasions and participated
prominently in the movement against the Ershad regime.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.abulkalamazad.info/about
 |title=Abul Kalam Azad – Full Biography
 |publisher=abulkalamazad.info
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

===Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami (1997–present)===

After concluding his student political career, Azad formally joined
[[Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami]] and rose through the party hierarchy:

* 1997–2011: Secretary, Khulna Metropolitan (14 years)
* 2012–2022: Amir (Chief), Khulna Metropolitan (10 years)
* 2023–present: Assistant Regional Director; Member, Central Executive Council

During his political career, he was imprisoned on multiple occasions
as a result of political reprisals.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.abulkalamazad.info/about
 |title=Abul Kalam Azad – Full Biography
 |publisher=abulkalamazad.info
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

==2026 General Election==

Voting for Khulna-6 was conducted on 12 February 2026, across 155 polling
centres in Koyra and Paikgacha upazilas, from 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM,
in a peaceful environment.<ref>{{cite news
 |url=https://dailyinqilab.com/bangladesh/news/863551
 |title=খুলনা-৬ আসনে জামায়াতের আবুল কালাম আজাদ বেসরকারিভাবে নির্বাচিত
 |trans-title=Jamaat's Abul Kalam Azad unofficially elected in Khulna-6
 |newspaper=Daily Inqilab
 |date=13 February 2026
 |access-date=18 May 2026
 |language=bn
}}</ref>

Azad secured 1,50,724 votes, defeating his nearest rival, [[Bangladesh Nationalist Party]]
(BNP) candidate SM Monirul Hasan, who received 1,24,710 votes.<ref>{{cite news
 |url=https://www.bssnews.net/national-parlament-election-2026/360817
 |title=Jamaat's Abul Kalam Azad wins unofficially from Khulna 6
 |publisher=Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha
 |date=13 February 2026
 |access-date=18 May 2026
}}</ref>

The margin of victory was 25,443 votes. Total valid votes cast were 2,27,418,
with 16,195 votes declared invalid.<ref>{{cite news
 |url=https://www.dhakaprotidin.com/%E0%A6%96%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A7%AC-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0/
 |title=খুলনা-৬ আসনে জামায়াত প্রার্থী মাও: আবুল কালাম আজাদ বিজয়ী
 |trans-title=Jamaat candidate Maw. Abul Kalam Azad victorious in Khulna-6
 |newspaper=Dhaka Protidin
 |date=14 February 2026
 |access-date=18 May 2026
 |language=bn
}}</ref>
